messages.snippet: Dear Ms Patel, Without prejudice. The court has directed the parties to consider ADR by 30 September
messages.subject: Pennington v Crossfield — ADR (without prejudice)
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Ms Patel,

Without prejudice. The court has directed the parties to consider ADR by 30 September. Our client is willing to mediate and we suggest a one-day mediation in September, after exchange of expert reports so both sides can take a clear view. Would your client agree in principle, and do you have any preferred mediators? We have used the panel at IPOS and at CEDR.

Kind regards,
Sarah Whitfield

--
Whitfield Carter LLP
22 Bishopsgate, London EC2N 4BQ
DX 138760 Cheapside | +44 (0)20 7946 0991
www.whitfieldcarter.com
This email is confidential and may be legally privileged.

messages.subject: RE: Pennington v Crossfield — ADR (without prejudice)
messages.plaintextBody:
Dear Ms Whitfield,

Without prejudice. Our client is content to mediate and agrees that after expert exchange makes sense. A September date is acceptable. We would be happy with a CEDR mediator; perhaps each side proposes two names and we agree from the overlap. We reserve our position on clause 11 in the meantime.

Kind regards,
Deepa Patel

--
Calderbank Hughes LLP | 5 Temple Gardens, London EC4Y 9AU
